headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error risks: Replit Agent can read/write and egress from shared Repl workspaces, while awesome-selfhosted is a static docs-only list with no runtime safeguards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write Repl files and execute shell commands, so only a manual copy-paste or file-bridge style injection path is plausible. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A’s repository or docs workflow, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF A is repurposed into a runtime service with an input parser, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference list only.
Do not paste untrusted B output into any downstream prompt.
Review any generated markdown before publishing.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels if A is embedded into a workflow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration, and it has broad network egress plus filesystem access. A is docs-only and does not itself process data, but if B’s workspace contains sensitive material, B can expose it externally. The pair’s interaction is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the Repl workspace, B can read them and transmit them over network egress.
IF A is used as a source of copied content into B prompts, that content can be retained in B’s context and outputs.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the Repl workspace.
Store credentials only in the secrets manager.
Disable or restrict outbound network where possible.
Audit generated files before sharing externally.
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive projects into separate Repls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot conflict operationally. B can write the Repl filesystem and modify git state, and Replit workspaces persist across sessions, so concurrent instances can overwrite each other’s changes. Because A is non-runnable, the conflict is one-sided but still real for B’s shared workspace.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same Repl, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF A is converted into a writable artifact inside the same workspace, it can be overwritten by B.
mitigations: Use one B instance per Repl.
Commit or stash changes before switching tasks.
Avoid parallel edits to the same files.
Lock critical files manually during edits.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can treat copied content as authoritative and act on it by editing files or committing changes, while A is a static knowledge list that may be used as a source of recommendations. If A-derived content is pasted into B without verification, B can propagate errors into code or deployment artifacts. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A’s recommendations are copied into B prompts or tasks, B may act on them without independent verification.
IF B is instructed to implement changes from A-derived text, errors can cascade into files or git history.
mitigations: Verify A-derived claims before acting on them.
Require a second review for code or deployment edits.
Keep A as reference only, not as an execution source.
Check diffs before commit.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while A is a public open-source knowledge-management resource with no data-handling controls. If regulated or confidential data is placed into B’s workspace, the mismatch between B’s cloud processing and A’s public-doc context creates a compliance gap. A is not cited for residency, so the risk is driven mainly by B.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into the Repl workspace, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator relies on A for policy guidance, it does not enforce retention or residency controls.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the Repl workspace.
Confirm data-processing terms for the Replit account.
Use separate environments for regulated projects.
Review retention settings before upload.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or approved hosting arrangement.
